g.text: IF YOU'RE SO SMART, WHY ARE YOU NOT · FIT / ATHLETIC · PART 4.0
Strength (mTOR) and endurance (AMPK) fight only when they peak at once. Keep the peaks apart.
DUAL TRACE · SHARED TIME AXIS · mTOR vs AMPK
CITE: 10 × 6-s max sprints, 15 min before a lift → mTOR activation completely abolished. A moderate cycle bout → no interference.

svg.text: INTENSITY, NOT DURATION, FIRES AMPK HARDEST

g.text: Cardio hurts strength more than strength hurts cardio.
So almost every rule points one way: protect the lift.
FIVE CONTROLS · ONE JOB: NEVER LET BOTH SIGNALS PEAK AT ONCE
Separate sessions ≥ 6 h · priority first. Forced same-session? Lift first.
1–2 hard intervals/wk MAX · pile on Zone 2 — the free cardio.
If you lift and want cardio: ride or row your Zone 2 — don't run it.
Wilson 2012 — RT+running blunted size AND strength; RT+cycling did not.
Glycogen refills in DAYS, not hours. Carbs around hard work · don't train hard fasted.
CONTROL 5 · THE SINGLE MOST EFFECTIVE CONTROL
8–12 wk blocks, then swap. Hold VO₂ ≈ 3×30 min/wk · hold strength ≈ 2 hard sets/muscle.
IS IT WORKING? — READ BOTH DASHBOARDS
BOTH move → paying the tax efficiently
ONE stalls → bias is wrong · re-program
BOTH stall + RHR↑ → deload, don't re-program
ENHANCED? AAS raises the recovery ceiling, not the biology. Same rules — more volume tolerance.
